arxiv-2404-11246.title: Learning Social Navigation from Demonstrations with Deep Neural Networks
arxiv-2404-11246.creator: Yigit Yildirim, Emre Ugur
arxiv-2404-11246.description: Abstract Traditional path planning techniques treat humans as obstacles. This has changed since robots started to enter human environments. On modern robots, social navigation has become an important aspect of navigation systems. To use learning-based techniques to achieve social navigation, a powerful framework that is capable of representing complex functions with as few data as possible is required.

arxiv-2406-10557.title: Explain the Black Box for the Sake of Science: the Scientific Method in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence
arxiv-2406-10557.creator: Gianmarco Mengaldo
arxiv-2406-10557.description: Abstract The scientific method is the cornerstone of human progress across all branches of the natural and applied sciences, from understanding the human body to explaining how the universe works. The scientific method is based on identifying systematic rules or principles that describe the phenomenon of interest in a reproducible way that can be validated through experimental evidence.

arxiv-2410-16666.title: QuasiNav : Asymmetric Cost-Aware Navigation Planning with Constrained Quasimetric Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2410-16666.creator: Jumman Hossain, Abu-Zaher Faridee, Derrik Asher, Jade Freeman, Theron Trout, Timothy Gregory, and Nirmalya Roy
arxiv-2410-16666.description: Abstract Autonomous navigation in unstructured outdoor environments is inherently challenging due to the presence of asymmetric traversal costs, such as varying energy expenditures for uphill versus downhill movement. Traditional reinforcement learning methods often assume symmetric costs, which can lead to suboptimal navigation paths and increased safety risks in real-world scenarios.

arxiv-2410-18008.title: Birational geometry of blowups via Weyl chamber decompositions and actions on curves
arxiv-2410-18008.creator: Maria Chiara Brambilla, Olivia Dumitrescu, Elisa Postinghel, Luis José Santana Sánchez
arxiv-2410-18008.description: Abstract . We study the birational geometry of X s n X^{n}_{s} , the blow-up of ℙ ℂ n \mathbb{P}^{n}_{\mathbb{C}} at s s points in general position. We identify a set of subvarieties, which we call Weyl r r -planes, that belong to an orbit for the action of the Weyl group on r r -cycles.

arxiv-2501-14704.title: Stroke classification using Virtual Hybrid Edge Detection from in silico electrical impedance tomography data
arxiv-2501-14704.creator: Juan Pablo Agnelli, Fernando S. Moura, Siiri Rautio, Melody Alsaker, Rashmi Murthy, Matti Lassas, Samuli Siltanen
arxiv-2501-14704.description: Abstract Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) is a non-invasive imaging method for recovering the internal conductivity of a physical body from electric boundary measurements. EIT combined with machine learning has shown promise for the classification of strokes. However, most previous works have used raw EIT voltage data as network inputs.

arxiv-2503-11778.title: The Power of the Cosmic Web
arxiv-2503-11778.creator: James Sunseri, Adrian E. Bayer, Jia Liu
arxiv-2503-11778.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by James Sunseri, Adrian E. Bayer, Jia Liu. We study the cosmological information contained in the cosmic web, categorized as four structure types: nodes, filaments, walls, and voids, using the Quijote simulations and a modified nexus+ algorithm. We show that splitting the density field by the four structure types and combining the power spectrum in each provides much tighter constraints on cosmological parameters than using the power spectrum without splitting.

arxiv-2505-15501.title: Protoknowledge Shapes Behaviour of LLMs in Downstream Tasks: Memorization and Generalization with Knowledge Graphs
arxiv-2505-15501.creator: Federico Ranaldi, Andrea Zugarini, Leonardo Ranaldi, Fabio Massimo Zanzotto
arxiv-2505-15501.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Federico Ranaldi, Andrea Zugarini, Leonardo Ranaldi, Fabio Massimo Zanzotto. We introduce the concept of protoknowledge to formalize and measure how sequences of tokens encoding Knowledge Graphs are internalized during pretraining and utilized at inference time by Large Language Models (LLMs). Indeed, LLMs have demonstrated the ability to memorize vast amounts of token sequences during pretraining, and a central open question is how they leverage this memorization as reusable knowledge through generalization.

arxiv-2509-11677.title: Measurement of beam-polarized Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering observables with the CLAS12 detector at Jefferson Lab
arxiv-2509-11677.creator: \firstname Juan Sebastian \lastname Alvarado \fnsep, \firstname Mostafa \lastname Hoballah \fnsep, \firstname Eric \lastname Voutier \fnsep
arxiv-2509-11677.description: Abstract In the context of nucleon structure studies, Generalized Parton Distributions (GPDs) are crucial for understanding the correlation between the longitudinal momentum and the transverse position of partons inside the nucleon. A privileged channel for GPD studies is the Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering (DVCS) process, whose experimental observables can provide access to GPDs through spin-dependent asymmetries.

pmc-11357583.description: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a highly aggressive and fatal primary brain tumor. pmc-12430061.title: Enhancing the Resistance to Shear Instability in Cu/Zr Nanolaminates Through Amorphous Interfacial Layer
pmc-12430061.creator: Feihu Chen, Feng Qin, Rossana Dimitri
pmc-12430061.description: Metallic nanolaminates generally show ultra-high strength but low ductility due to their vulnerability to shear instability during deformation. Herein, we report the simultaneous enhancement in hardness (by 11.9%) and suppression of shear instability in a 10 nm Cu/Zr nanolaminate, achieved by introducing a nanoscale Cu63Zr37 amorphous interfacial layer (AIL) between the crystalline Cu and Zr layers via magnetron sputtering.

uslaw-usc-t49-s30171.title: 49 U.S.C. § 30171 — Protection of employees providing motor vehicle safety information
uslaw-usc-t49-s30171.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t49-s30171.description: United States Code, Title 49 (Transportation); Part A (General); Chapter 301 (Motor Vehicle Safety); Subchapter IV (Enforcement And Administrative). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Discrimination Against Employees of Manufacturers, Part Suppliers, and Dealerships.— No motor vehicle manufacturer, part supplier, or dealership may discharge an employee or otherwise discriminate against an employee with respect to compensation, terms, conditions, or privileges of employment.
